To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a model for analyzing interpretability in relation to specific roles and that we illustrated its use in a variety of contexts, showing that an agent's role has implications for its goals and for defining interpretability.

1) a machine learning system’s interpretability should be evaluated in relation to a particular role; 2) the role determines the agent’s goals, which in turn determine the relevant criteria for evaluating the system; and 3) the role also affects the agent’s ability to use the system, which in turn affects the agent’s goals.

we have developed a model for understanding the role-based definition of interpretability and we have illustrated the model in several scenarios to show how it can be used to understand the definition of interpretability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do we define interpretability in relation to a particular agent?
the following problem: How do different agents interact with a machine learning system, and how does this influence what they consider to be interpretable about the system?
how interpretability should be measured and defined, and we hope to encourage further discussion of this question.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is a useful tool for analyzing interpretability in machine learning systems.
the model is a useful tool for understanding how interpretability should be evaluated, but it is not a panacea for all problems.
there is no one definition of interpretability, but there are many.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of the audience should be considered in the design of the machine learning systems, as well as in the evaluation of interpretability.
the role of an agent in relation to a ML system influences what it means for the ML system to be interpretable to that agent.
interpretability is a multi-faceted concept and that it is not enough to simply say that a model is interpretable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not think of interpretability as a binary characteristic of a machine learning system, but as a property that varies with the role of an agent in relation to that system.
there are many different perspectives on interpretability, and that the perspective we choose to adopt is a key part of our definition of interpretability.
interpretability is not a property of the machine learning system, but of the relationship between the system and the agent who interacts with it.
